candidates.severity: unassigned; repeated private admission, with no observed canonical-value failure
candidates.classification: 95e revisit of the same earlier Lens12 contract, not a new unique historical defect.
candidates.trace: hostile_group_authority_row parses enemy_type through parse_threat into the existing catalog-backed ThreatId and reads its escalation profile. Before constructing the native row it passes the original string to private autoresolve_drop, which calls parse_threat again and reads the profile loot item. The eventual native HostileGroupAuthority stores enemy_type and optional loot item as strings; the repeated private parse precedes that storage boundary. Source-only exact-spelling search also found the private helper used directly for a standalone bandit row and the resolved native encounter archetype; these callers have different input boundaries and cannot simply be deleted. Errantry passes the authored armed_retainer literal to the materializer. No wrong loot, invalid canonical variant or product incident is asserted.
candidates.connected_repair: After audit completion, carry a correctly admitted catalog threat or its selected profile through the private row and loot helper; convert at the final native storage boundary. Admit literal, native and other private callers at their real boundaries, preserve no-loot and unsupported encounter-archetype cases, count/difficulty normalization, unknown-input rejection and runtime error/transaction behavior.
candidates.discovery: partial; all callers, roster/loot consumers, transaction semantics, exact aliases and independent lenses remain open

candidates.severity: unassigned; typed generated identity becomes a string before a private helper and is parsed again
candidates.classification: 95e revisit of the same earlier Lens12 contract, not a new unique historical defect; related to but not automatically an alias of the separate drop-helper finding.
candidates.trace: GeneratedCase.hostile_groups is a vector containing existing ThreatId values. materialize_generated_quest passes each threat.as_str().into() into private materialize_hostile_group; its row helper subsequently parses the string through catalog-backed FromStr before computing the profile and only then writing a native row. The generated and drop-helper roundtrips are distinct producer/helper boundaries even though one connected repair may touch both. DeveloperGenerationContext and normal generation are distinct origins; the inspected DeveloperQuestDefinition also contains ThreatId.
candidates.admission_caveat: ThreatId::try_new validates syntax but does not ensure a catalog entry; FromStr adds catalog lookup, and profile assumes the entry exists. Therefore replacing the selected parse with an arbitrary typed value could turn a rejected unknown into a profile failure. Determine and preserve the actual catalog-admission contract at each producer before carrying a value through the private graph; the separate L11 finding remains related, not an established alias.
candidates.connected_repair: After audit completion, use the existing catalog-admitted threat identity through generated materialization and row/profile/loot computation, encoding only for native fields. Trace every authored, native, incident, standalone, generated and developer caller and keep their real admission, error, no-loot, normalized count and transaction policies.
candidates.discovery: partial; generated admission, all group callers, aliases, roster, native consumers and independent lenses remain open

bounded_observations.question: Does selected road-choice presentation have the same predicate as the later action?
bounded_observations.disposition: The gateway projection marks blocked choices unavailable and, for a treatment-backed choice, uses the presence of a bandaged patient wound rather than checking the remaining requirements. Other choices use their declared requirements; the reducer separately checks all applicable requirements and all authored checks after requiring treatment. The wounded knight treatment choice includes a physiology check and a bandage requirement; reducer intentionally skips the bandage requirement and consume effect after ordinary treatment, avoiding a second cost. The courier aid choice has no listed additional requirement or check. For non-treatment religion choices the view uses finite positive direct study hours while the reducer computes a health- and aptitude-limited religion check, including the authored difficulty. The web template enables the submit button using the projection boolean. A button may therefore be available while a later check fails; whether availability promises successful checks, and the actual admitted character/camp conditions, are unestablished. This is a policy question, not an asserted product failure.
bounded_observations.qualification: Selected authored source and source-only view/reducer/template inspection; no catalog build, character state, action or UI executed.

bounded_observations.question: Does a typed narrative ReligionId silently select among several currently authored religions?
bounded_observations.disposition: The inspected catalog ReligionId has exactly the RomanCatholic variant, and narrative_religion returns OfficialReligion::RomanCatholic. The current closed set therefore gives no supported different-variant counterexample, although a match would make future extension explicit.
bounded_observations.qualification: Bounded current source observation, not a complete catalog or admission review.
